open_points.subject: artifact pointer writer
open_points.text: “A service publishes and withdraws none” contradicts “a producer publishes `uri`, `payload_ref` and digest without them.”
open_points.question: Who writes the pointer values: the agent or owner publishing through Registry, or the producer service?
options: The agent or owner writes them; the producer service only holds the document
The producer service writes them despite not publishing the pointer
The producer supplies them to Kernel, which publishes them as the agent
open_points.default_guess: The agent or owner writes them; the producer service only holds the document.

open_points.subject: publish request-id collision
open_points.text: “a retried publish — the same request id — is not a second publish and returns the pointer it made”
open_points.question: What happens when the same request id is submitted again with different type, project, URI, payload reference, digest, or other content?
options: Refuse it as conflicting reuse of a request id
Return the pointer created by the first request and ignore the changed content
Treat it as a new publish
open_points.default_guess: Refuse it as conflicting reuse of a request id.

open_points.subject: owner publish replay
open_points.text: “As a write of the agent, a publish carries a request id” while the publish action also names “the owner”
open_points.question: Does an owner publication also carry a request id, and what observable result follows if the owner retries it after losing the answer?
options: The owner also supplies a request id and receives the original pointer on retry
Only agent publications carry request ids; an owner retry creates a new version
The owner interface uses a different replay-prevention input and behavior
open_points.default_guess: Only agent publications carry request ids; an owner retry creates a new version.

open_points.subject: publish replay after later pointer changes
open_points.text: “its retry returns the pointer it made”
open_points.question: If that pointer has since been superseded or withdrawn, does retrying the original request return the original publish response, return the pointer with its current status, or fail?
options: Return the original publish response with status `published`
Return the same pointer with its current status
Refuse because the pointer is no longer published
open_points.default_guess: Return the original publish response with status `published`.
